authority_levels.approve: Executor posts the step and waits for an analyst to approve it.
authority_levels.recommend_only: Executor writes the step into the plan and never dispatches it.

eradication.note: The analyst executes these through the action surface, so the framework still times the phase and MTTE stays measured.

recovery.note: reverse_only_live_actions keeps recovery off entries the ledger recorded as shadow, which never happened and so cannot be undone.

rules.name: malicious_high_confidence
rules.reason: Assessment returned a malicious verdict at high confidence

elevate.note: Any matching rule elevates the case; conditions inside a rule are AND'd via `requires`. Deliberately conservative - a star cannot be undone by the framework and a starred case is exempt from auto-close, so the bar is a malicious verdict at high confidence. escalate_recommended was removed as a star condition: the prompt itself warns it must not merely restate the verdict, and on a Turla Carbon replay it was true on 53 of 60 assessed issues against 48 malicious - so it only ever loosened the bar, adding one case that had no malicious issue at all. Measured on that replay, malicious-at-high-confidence starred exactly the five cases carrying real attack activity and left the unrelated AIRS and AWS findings alone. RAISE ONLY on severity - the framework never lowers one. An absent field never matches. Operators: eq, in, gte.

ticketing.note: Ticket scope is the case. Per-issue tickets rebuild the alert storm that case grouping exists to remove.
